MN-2025-HF1141.s: The law makes changes to Minnesota housing finance rules and gives money for housing programs. It sets aside $10 million for supportive housing and $25 million in fiscal year 2027 for programs like workforce housing, manufactured home park aid, family homeless prevention, renter legal help, and homebuyer education. It also changes some agency rules on funds, investment earnings, meetings, reports, and housing bonds.

MN-2025-HF1410.s: The law changes discipline rules for correctional officers and peace officers in Minnesota. It adds steps for written complaints, witness lists, access to reports, recording of statement sessions, and the right to have a union representative or lawyer present. It also lets an officer seek actual damages, costs, and attorney fees if a state or local agency breaks these rules. It takes effect August 1, 2026.

MN-2025-HF1606.s: This law prohibits websites, apps, and similar services from letting users alter or make images or videos to show fake nude or sexual body parts of a real, identifiable person. It also bans advertising or promoting services that do this, and it lets the person shown in the image sue for damages, court orders, and legal fees. The attorney general can enforce the law, and it takes effect August 1, 2026.

MN-2025-HF1849.s: The bill would ask voters to change the Minnesota Constitution to limit the governor and lieutenant governor to two elected terms each. It would put the question on the 2026 general election ballot. Earlier elections would not count toward the term limit.

MN-2025-HF2133.s: The bill would make a technical fix to Minnesota’s pass-through entity tax rules. It would keep the credit for tax paid to another state and clarify how the term is used for partnerships, limited liability companies, and S corporations. The change would take effect the day after final passage.

MN-2025-HF2354.s: The bill would add a new crime for medical assistance fraud and update state law on how it is handled. It would give the attorney general more power to subpoena records tied to medical assistance fraud cases, including phone, banking, insurance, and wage records. It would also change related laws so the attorney general or county attorney can bring criminal or civil cases under these rules.

MN-2025-HF2358.s: The law increases criminal penalties for some coercion crimes, which are threats used to force someone to act. If the coercion leads to great bodily harm, the penalty can be up to 10 years in prison and a $20,000 fine. If it leads to death, the penalty can be up to 15 years in prison and a $30,000 fine. It took effect on August 1, 2026.

MN-2025-HF2433.s: The law changes how some K-12 education aid is figured and used in 2027 and 2028. It also requires school districts and charter schools to adopt an anonymous threat reporting system by June 30, 2027, and use either a local system or the state system by July 1, 2028. Schools must share information about the system with students, families, and staff, and the education commissioner must report which schools have chosen each option. It also creates grant money for these reporting systems and requires reports on their use.

MN-2025-HF2438.s: The bill became law as Chapter 128. It deals with taxes and with how state and local government are funded and run. It also relates to the Public Safety Department and transportation agencies.

MN-2025-HF2484.s: The law sets aside general fund money in fiscal year 2027 for capital projects, including one-time spending rules for state-funded construction work. It gives $4.5 million to Minnesota State Colleges and Universities, with $3 million for tearing down old buildings and fixing sites, and $1.5 million for space and programs at Winona State University for a legislative engagement center. It also sets rules for grant recipients, requires prevailing wages on covered projects, and makes sustainable building rules apply to state-funded new buildings and major renovations.

MN-2025-HF3067.s: The law clarifies how school paraprofessionals can meet job qualification rules. It says districts and charter schools can confirm certain skills and keep records of that proof in the worker's file. The change took effect on May 20, 2026.

MN-2025-HF3298.s: The new law sets up a state reimbursement program for underground petroleum storage tank systems with pressurized single-walled steel piping. For replacement projects that start after January 1, 2027, the board must pay 50% of the cost for certain eligible equipment and related work, up to $100,000 per location, with a yearly cap of $4 million from the fund. It applies to tank systems in Minnesota that meet the bill's rules, and the program expires June 30, 2037.

MN-2025-HF3404.s: This law raises the penalty for pretending to be a peace officer, and it adds a new crime for doing that while carrying a firearm. It also adds tougher penalties if someone commits another crime while pretending to be an officer. In some cases, officers must give their agency name, last name, and ID number, and the law takes effect August 1, 2026.

MN-2025-HF3426.s: This law sets money rules for the Environment and Natural Resources Trust Fund, which helps pay for work on the environment and natural resources. It took effect on May 19, 2026.

MN-2025-HF3437.s: The law changes how some fees and penalties apply to certain home loans used for investment property. It creates a definition for a DSCR loan, which is a mortgage based on expected rent or cash flow from the property instead of the borrower's personal income. The change takes effect August 1, 2026, and applies to residential mortgage loans made on or after that date.

MN-2025-HF3453.s: The law raises the legal age to buy or possess kratom in Minnesota to 21. Selling kratom to someone under 21 is a gross misdemeanor, and a person under 21 who has kratom is guilty of a misdemeanor. It took effect on August 1, 2026.

MN-2025-HF3489.s: Minnesota enacted a law that requires schools and related offices to report certain teacher and administrator cases to the right licensing board. It also creates a crime of grooming and sets criminal penalties for it. The law also makes other changes tied to child protection and appropriates money.

MN-2025-HF3521.s: Minnesota law would add an exception to the rule that limits new hospital construction and some hospital bed changes. It affects hospitals and health care facilities and lists several specific projects and locations that could move ahead, including some bed additions and replacements. The law took effect on August 1, 2026.

MN-2025-HF3544.s: The law says some veterans and former service members who lost federal benefits do not qualify for state-funded veterans benefits, services, or programs in Minnesota. It also ends the state program that gave veterans information and help about environmental hazards like chemical agents. The law took effect on August 1, 2026.

MN-2025-HF3579.s: The bill would let eggs be donated after their quality assurance date if they stay in their original pack, were already checked and graded, and are kept cold. Charitable food assistance programs could give out those eggs for up to 30 days after that date, with a label saying they are donated eggs and not for resale. It also keeps the current rule that retail eggs must be removed from sale after set time limits based on the pack date.

MN-2025-HF3676.s: This law changes Minnesota’s Safe at Home program, which helps some people keep their address private. It updates who can apply, adds rules for guardians applying for minors or incapacitated people, and changes how the secretary of state handles contact and mail information. It also adds limits on when a participant’s real address can be forced into court cases and sets criminal penalties for some violations. The law took effect on August 1, 2026.

MN-2025-HF3709.s: The law lets banks and credit unions offer virtual-currency custody services, which means safekeeping or managing virtual currency or the private keys used to access it. They must notify the commissioner 60 days before starting, keep written safety, security, and compliance policies, and keep customer virtual currency separate from their own assets. The commissioner may review these services and may limit them if they are unsafe or unsound. It takes effect August 1, 2026.

MN-2025-HF3718.s: Minnesota made changes to the rules for veterinary medicine and veterinary technology. The law updates who and what is covered under those rules, and it affects veterinarians, veterinary technicians, and people who care for animals. It took effect on July 1, 2026.

MN-2025-HF3825.s: The law changes licensing and practice rules for several health jobs in Minnesota, including acupuncture, herbal medicine, athletic training, social work, dentistry, pharmacy, physical therapy, and advanced practice registered nursing. It also creates registration for massage therapists and Asian bodywork therapists, and licenses music therapists. The law also makes other rule changes, sets up advisory councils, allows civil penalties, requires reports, adds fees, and includes money for these changes.

MN-2025-HF3827.s: The law changes crime data rules, makes state money for some local criminal investigations and witness protection count as reimbursements, and updates how crime reports are recorded. It also puts more orders for protection into the law enforcement data system and requires a photo to go with a no-contact order when one is available and verified by the court.

MN-2025-HF3970.s: The law creates a court process that lets an unmarried person who is a buyer in a contract for deed ask to end the other buyer’s interest if that person has caused domestic abuse, sexual assault, sexual extortion, or harassment and has left the property. It sets rules for filing the case, serving notice, and what proof can be used. The law was approved on May 7, 2026, and takes effect July 1, 2026.

MN-2025-HF4052.s: Minnesota changed several rules for telephone companies. The law updates filing and reporting rules, limits some extra reporting for local exchange carriers and competitive local exchange carriers, and requires carriers to have equipment that can support lawful police wiretaps and call data access. It also changes some rules on prices, service labels, and inspections of company books and property.

MN-2025-HF4063.s: The law changes rules for school buses in Minnesota. It lets school buses be used for driver training, requires a USDOT number for school bus tracking, and changes first aid kit rules for newer buses, with all type III buses required to have the newer kit by January 1, 2030. It also limits some school bus warning equipment on public roads when a bus is used by a licensed commercial driver training school.

MN-2025-HF4074.s: This law changes retirement rules for some public workers, including corrections staff, firefighters, and other state and public employees. It affects retirement benefits and related pension policies for those groups.

MN-2025-HF4090.s: The bill would change prize and ticket limits for paddlewheel gambling in Minnesota. It would keep the top cash prize at $70, set the top fair market value for a merchandise prize at $200, and raise the highest ticket price from $2 to $5. It affects groups that run this type of lawful gambling and people who buy paddle tickets.

MN-2025-HF4102.s: The bill would change how often the State Patrol pay study is done and what it covers. It would also let the State Patrol recruit and use unpaid volunteer chaplains, and let the chief supervisor cover their travel, lodging, and meal costs. It would also change how some pay rules for State Patrol ranks are handled.

MN-2025-HF4118.s: Credit unions in Minnesota would be allowed to get insurance from a credit union share insurance provider. The law also sets rules for credit union share guaranty corporations and makes related changes to state law. It became law as Chapter 56 and takes effect on August 1, 2026.

MN-2025-HF4133.s: Minnesota law now says homeowners insurance cannot leave out coverage for certain property damage caused by a peace officer using chemical irritants, smoke screens, or diversionary devices when the homeowner is owed just compensation. It also lets the homeowner choose the repair contractor and, if needed, an industrial hygienist to check and fix the damage. The law takes effect January 1, 2027, and applies to policies offered, issued, or renewed on or after that date.

MN-2025-HF4188.s: This commerce policy bill became law in Minnesota. It affects the Commerce Department and consumer protection rules.

MN-2025-HF4239.s: The law changes Minnesota campaign finance rules on noncampaign spending, which is money a campaign committee can use for listed non-election purposes. It also changes how certain data is classified, how complaints are handled, and the rules for reports, written messages, and disclaimer statements. The changes affect candidates, campaign committees, and related election groups.

MN-2025-HF4240.s: Minnesota law changes election administration rules, including absentee voting steps and deadlines. It also bars elected officials and candidates from betting on elections and makes other technical updates. The law includes an appropriation of money.

MN-2025-HF4252.s: This law changes several higher education rules in Minnesota. It updates student aid reports, limits some student fees for athletic facilities, allows a land lease for Rochester Community and Technical College, and changes rules for American Indian Scholars, private career schools, and some private and out-of-state public colleges. It also expands paid blood donation leave for Minnesota State employees, requires priority registration for pregnant and parenting students, and includes money for higher education.

MN-2025-HF4384.s: The bill would change Minnesota child care training rules on abusive head trauma, which is harm to a baby or young child from shaking. It would require the training to be interactive, not just reading or watching material. The rules would apply to child care center directors, staff, substitutes, volunteers, and some family child care workers, and the changes would take effect January 1, 2027.

MN-2025-HF4492.s: The law changes Minnesota’s Read Act rules for early reading checks in schools and updates terms used in the law. It also requires some teacher candidates to have early literacy field experience, creates a high school diploma option for veterans, and calls for new rules to carry out the changes. The bill became law as Chapter 125 in 2026.

MN-2025-HF4591.s: The law makes changes to state government spending and operations in Minnesota. It covers the Legislature, state finance and administration, the Board of the Arts, the Board of Barber Examiners, and the Board of Cosmetology Examiners. It also creates the Melissa and Mark Hortman Memorial State Park Working Group, sets some fees, and requires a report.

MN-2025-HF5074.s: The law sets aside state money to pay certain claims and settlement awards. It gives $250,000 to James Lamar Davis, $350,000 to Clayton Douglas Groves, and $4.5 million to Marvin Haynes under the state law for people who were wrongly imprisoned. It also gives $4,570.40 to Mark Carroll for injuries tied to correctional work or time in a state prison. The law took effect on July 1, 2026.

MN-2025-HF5125.s: The bill would end the sales tax break for data centers and remove a planned cut to special education aid. It would also update the state rules for what counts as a large data center and who can get refunds for certain taxes, with those changes effective July 1, 2026.

MN-2025-HF5150.s: Public cemeteries would have to allow people to be buried according to the rites of their recognized religion. They would also have to allow green burials, which means a more natural burial method. The rules would apply to municipalities, towns, and other cemeteries covered by state law, if the burial follows the state rules for burial and green burials.

MN-2025-HF5152.s: The bill would let a person ask to change or add a sex indicator on a birth record, and it would let certain people request the same kind of change on a death record. It would also let some marriage records be modified and would make older replaced records private data that can be shared only by court order. The commissioner would have to offer at least three sex marker choices, including an "X."

MN-2025-HF5154.s: The bill would create a new office in the Department of Agriculture to look at agriculture business concentration and farm land buying trends in Minnesota. It would also require the office to send a report every two years to lawmakers who handle agriculture. The agriculture commissioner would appoint a director and hire staff, and the bill would set aside an unspecified amount of general fund money in fiscal year 2027 for the office.

MN-2025-HF5156.s: The bill would set rules for certain prescription drugs that have a federal "maximum fair price," which is the highest price set by the U.S. government. It would bar drug makers from charging more than that price in Minnesota and would require health plans and pharmacy benefit managers to pay at least that amount, or the national average drug acquisition cost if higher, plus dispensing fees. It would also limit drug makers from pulling these drugs from the state to avoid the price rules and set a penalty for doing so. The section would take effect January 1, 2027.

MN-2025-HF5157.s: The bill would make it a crime to create, have, or share a nudification image without the person’s consent. A nudification image is a picture, video, or other visual recording that has been changed to show a real person as nude or with intimate parts when the original did not. It would apply to people who make or share these images, and it would take effect August 1, 2026.

MN-2025-HF5159.s: The bill would bar permits for nonferrous metallic mining in the Rainy River headwaters unless the mine is not expected to raise sulfate levels in water by more than zero parts per million, and it would require water monitoring to be posted online. If a mine causes a sulfate increase above that level, the commissioner of natural resources would have to order work to stop and assess a $500 million civil penalty. Mining could restart only after three years of approved water-quality monitoring shows the problem was fixed and future mining would stay within the same sulfate limit. The mine operator would have to give access for the monitoring and pay all related costs.

MN-2025-HF719.s: Minnesota made this law, and it provides funding for a safe routes to school grant program by issuing bonds and setting aside state money. The program affects children and minors who travel to school.

MN-2025-SF1714.s: State contracting agencies would have to give contractors and subcontractors payment details for public improvement jobs after a written request. The info would include the payment amount, the date it was made or approved, and a copy of the payment form, and it would have to be provided within seven days at no charge. Agencies would also have to post contact info for these requests, and the law took effect on August 1, 2026.

MN-2025-SF1943.s: The bill would ban pet shops from selling cats and dogs in Minnesota. It affects pet shops and the people who buy pets from them. The bill passed.

MN-2025-SF2077.s: The measure is an omnibus bill about Minnesota outdoor heritage fund, legacy, and land issues. It would affect state natural resources and related funding and land programs. It became law as Chapter 126 on May 27, 2026.

MN-2025-SF2082.s: Would change Minnesota transportation policy and set money for transportation programs and the transportation department.

MN-2025-SF2814.s: Minnesota made this law for real estate appraisers. It lets the commissioner use the current Appraisal Foundation sanction matrix as nonbinding guidance when setting discipline, while still deciding each case based on its own facts. It took effect on August 1, 2026.

MN-2025-SF3210.s: The law adds a rule that not trying to work out a reasonable accommodation for a person with a disability may count as unfair discrimination. It applies to employment, housing, public accommodations, public services, and education. The law took effect on August 1, 2026.

MN-2025-SF334.s: The law creates a Human Services Systems Modernization Advisory Council and a Legislative Commission on Human Services Systems in Minnesota. The council gives advice on the planning, funding, and updating of human services computer systems used by counties, tribes, and state agencies, and it must report to the legislature at least once a year. It also creates a modernization fund and sets rules for money transfers into that fund.

MN-2025-SF3432.s: This law gives money for public safety and security work in Minnesota. It covers the Department of Public Safety, corrections, courts, the Legislature, and some constitutional officers. It also includes changes on Capitol security, elected official contact info, clemency, and other public safety rules.

MN-2025-SF3602.s: The law creates rules for electronic estate planning papers in Minnesota, such as trusts, powers of attorney, advance directives, and some body-disposition forms. It defines terms like electronic record, electronic signature, and electronic presence, and says these papers can be handled electronically unless the document says no. It took effect on August 1, 2026.

MN-2025-SF3720.s: Adopts 2026 recommendations of the Workers' Compensation Advisory Council and changes several workers' compensation rules in Minnesota. It updates how the reinsurance association handles member withdrawals, insolvency, premiums, and reports. The law took effect the day after final enactment.

MN-2025-SF3887.s: Minnesota became law says towns, watershed districts, and watershed management organizations with more than 100 employees may self-insure for employee health benefits, including long-term disability, if they meet state rules. It also lets some of these public employers join together to do the same. The law adds notice and approval steps for plans with union-represented workers and takes effect August 1, 2026.

MN-2025-SF3888.s: The law lets tow trucks use a portable variable message sign while doing emergency service on or near a highway. The sign must meet state traffic control standards. It became law as Chapter 78 and takes effect on August 1, 2026.

MN-2025-SF3891.s: The law lets some eggs that are past their quality assurance date be donated to charitable food programs. The eggs must be in their original package, already checked and graded, kept cold, given out within 30 days after that date, and labeled with the charity name, a "distribute by" date, and "Donated Eggs - Not for Resale." It took effect on August 1, 2026.

MN-2025-SF390.s: The bill would set aside $10 million for grants in the safe routes to school program, which helps pay for safer ways for students to get to school. It would also let the state sell up to $10 million in bonds, which are borrowed money the state must pay back. The money would go to the transportation commissioner, and the section would take effect the day after final passage.

MN-2025-SF3958.s: The law changes the deadline for a yearly report on the disaster assistance contingency account from January 15 to January 31. That report goes to key budget lawmakers and covers disaster aid money set aside and spent in the prior year. It took effect on August 1, 2026.

MN-2025-SF3967.s: The bill would require health plans to cover home care nursing for people who are also on medical assistance, and it would bar plans from setting quantity limits on that coverage. It also says the state should not make payments to cover those benefits and must help support full coverage in the private market. Health plans would have to use the term "home care nursing services" for these services in their plan documents. The first two parts would apply back to January 1, 2026, and the labeling rule would start August 1, 2026.

MN-2025-SF4171.s: The law changes how landlords can send final utility bills to tenants who move out, including for submetered and apportioned utility charges. It also adds rules for rent payments through digital payment platforms, bans listing a tenant’s minor child as a defendant in most eviction cases, and expands the expedited eviction process to include assaults on landlords or their workers. Some parts apply to eviction cases filed on or after August 1, 2026, and the law takes effect on that date.

MN-2025-SF4244.s: Minnesota changed several small technical parts of state laws and statutes, affecting government and the legislature. It became law as Chapter 88 and takes effect August 1, 2026.

MN-2025-SF4282.s: This law makes forecast changes for the Education, Human Services, and Children, Youth, and Families departments, and for Metro Mobility. It also changes rules for school paraprofessionals, allows some school district fund transfers, and provides permanent school fund aid for Tribal contract schools. It became law in 2026 as Chapter 109 and includes money for these changes.

MN-2025-SF4339.s: The law changes Minnesota’s underground excavation notice system and adds an electronic positive response process. It requires operators to send electronic updates through the notification center for excavation and boundary survey notices, and to keep up-to-date contact information there. Most of the changes take effect August 1, 2026, and the contact information rule takes effect January 1, 2027.

MN-2025-SF4400.s: The bill would change rules for nonemergency medical transportation in Minnesota health care programs. Starting January 1, 2027, or later if federal approval is needed, providers would have to follow added state rules on top of current billing and service standards. It would also update who can be removed from the program and what data the state agency must report each month.

MN-2025-SF4401.s: It would make a broad set of changes to Minnesota's cannabis laws and related rules.

MN-2025-SF4476.s: The law provides extra funding for Minnesota human services programs. It became law as Chapter 121 and affects the state programs that deliver those services.

MN-2025-SF4515.s: The bill would change limits for paddle tickets in lawful gambling. It would raise the highest cash prize to $70, set the highest merchandise prize at a fair market value of $200, and raise the most an organization may charge for a paddle ticket to $5. It would also say gift cards that can be redeemed for cash do not count as merchandise prizes.

MN-2025-SF4612.s: This law provides supplemental funding for Minnesota health and human services programs. It affects the state Health Department and Human Services Department, along with the programs they run. It became Chapter 127 in the 2026 regular session.

MN-2025-SF4760.s: Creates a law on public safety policy and changes related to the Public Safety Department.

MN-2025-SF5200.s: The law makes a set of technical fixes to earlier Minnesota laws, including a correction to the rules for summary statement forms used in elections. It also sets new effective dates for parts of other laws on the Supreme Court Council on Child Protection and direct primary care service agreements. Unless a different date is given, each part takes effect when the law being corrected takes effect.

MN-2025-SF5306.s: The bill would give state grants for radar equipment and related work for local governments, including airport authorities and airport commissions. The money could go to radar sensors, towers, wiring, site work, training, and support for air and water surveillance, and the transportation commissioner would run the grants with the public safety commissioner. It would take effect the day after it is finally passed, and the money would come from the general fund in fiscal year 2027.

MN-2025-SF5307.s: The bill would change Minnesota rent rules so rent must be split up for an incomplete first month as well as an incomplete last month of a lease. It would apply to renters and landlords, and lease terms that try to waive these rules would be void. The change would take effect the day after final passage and apply to leases signed on or after that date.

MN-2025-SF5308.s: The bill would let certain retired police officers in Minnesota go back to work for a city and keep getting their retirement annuity without it being cut or stopped. It also would let them keep their state public employee health coverage during reemployment, with the worker usually paying for it unless a contract or policy says otherwise. Cities would face limits on how many of these reemployed retired officers they can hire, based on city size.

MN-2025-SF5309.s: The bill would create a new office in the Department of Agriculture to study farm business consolidation and farm land ownership in Minnesota. It would look at purchases of agricultural land by people, companies, churches, and other nonprofits, and would give advice to the agriculture commissioner. The office would also send a report every two years to lawmakers, and the bill would set aside money in fiscal year 2027 to start and run it.
